reviews.textTranslated: It's about 10km from National Highway 1A, a bit far but the road is easy to navigate. The restaurant is located right by Tam Giang Lagoon, with a very airy and cool seating area; it would be great if there were some hammocks. The food comes out quite quickly. Brown fish is the main specialty here and is very delicious. Besides that, the snails, clams, and mussels are also fresh and tasty. The prices aren't too expensive, but they're not cheap either. To eat comfortably, you'll probably need around 300-400k VND per person.

reviews.textTranslated: I was recommended this restaurant by a local, one of three located right on the Con Toc ferry terminal - Tam Giang Lagoon. However, I found the prices here to be reasonable, as I've eaten at the last branch I visited. They have a tank of fresh seafood for you to choose from. The dishes are served quickly and are attractively presented. My favorites were the Herring Salad and the Pickled Seaweed Salad. The crab with roe and green prawns are guaranteed to be delicious. One drawback is that the service is a bit slow, probably because the staff are new. Overall, it's definitely worth trying. The prices are reasonable for my budget.

After being recommended by our hotel, we decided to try this restaurant—just note that it’s located upstairs above another restaurant, so it can be a little easy to miss.

They offer both Vietnamese and Western food, but we stuck with the Vietnamese options. It’s located right opposite a nightclub, which actually made for some pretty entertaining people-watching while we dined. You can choose to sit outside or downstairs in air conditioning.

We started with the papaya salad, which was very good—served with peanuts and dried onions—though not quite as fresh as what we experienced during a cooking class in Hoi An. The standout dish was definitely the eggplant with garlic and butter—absolutely amazing and a must-order.

We also had the beef hot pot, which came with very rare slices of beef that you cook yourself, along with vegetables and rice noodles. It was a fun and interactive meal.

Overall, a really nice experience, and great value at around 350,000.

Bánh Mì Chu Văn An is an absolute must-visit if you want to experience what a real Vietnamese bánh mì should taste like. It’s a small, humble street stall — nothing fancy at all — but what comes out of that tiny setup is pure perfection.
I ordered the special bánh mì, and honestly, it was the best bánh mì I’ve ever had. It comes loaded with everything — different types of meats, pate, pickled vegetables, herbs, sauces — and the combination is just brutal. Every bite is perfectly balanced: crunchy bread, rich and savory fillings, and that signature mix of sweet, salty, and slightly tangy flavors that make Vietnamese sandwiches so unique.
The bread was perfectly toasted — light and crisp on the outside, soft and warm inside — and it held together beautifully without falling apart, even with all those delicious fillings. The ingredients were incredibly fresh, and the sauce tied everything together just right. You can tell this is made by someone who knows exactly what they’re doing.
The woman who runs the stall is one of the kindest and warmest people I’ve met while traveling in Vietnam. She was super friendly and welcoming, smiling the entire time and clearly proud of her food. Even though her English was limited, communication wasn’t a problem — her kindness said it all. You can feel the love and care she puts into every sandwich.
The price is also fantastic — incredibly cheap for the quality and size of the sandwich. It’s one of those meals that makes you stop and think, “How can something this good cost so little?” You could easily pay three times as much elsewhere and not come close to this level of flavor or satisfaction.
What I loved most was that this isn’t a tourist trap — it’s a genuine, local spot serving real food for real people. There’s no marketing gimmick, no fancy decor — just honest, homemade perfection.
If you only have time to try one bánh mì while in Vietnam, make it this one. The special is the way to go — it’s got a little bit of everything, and the combination is absolutely spot-on.
The location is easy to find, and even if you have to wait a few minutes during busy hours, it’s completely worth it. Everything is made fresh, right in front of you, and the result is unforgettable.
Overall, Bánh Mì Chu Văn An is everything you want in a Vietnamese street-food experience: incredible flavor, friendly people, and unbeatable value. The special bánh mì is out of this world — truly the best I’ve had anywhere.

As the name suggests, the cafe is located inside the famous Vi Da Hamlet. It is roomier than it looks with the backyard right next to the river, which offers a great view and calm asmotsphere.

I order one salted coffee and a set of imperial tea.

The coffee is great. The sweetness and saltiness of the cream complement the bitterness of the coffee, resulting in a sophisticated and well-rounded flavour profile.

Next is the tea set.
For an affordable price, this is one of the best tea experiences you can find. The brew features dried fruits and is served with a side of sweets to complement the flavors. Each sip offers a subtle bitterness and sweet aftertaste that finishes with a fragant herbal notes.

Last but not least, the employees are super friendly who carefully attend to your needs.

I have come here ever since I was young. It’s my favourite breakfast spot. A little on the more expensive side but the breakfast dishes are delicious. The yoghurt drinks are my favourite too. Hanh, our waitress gave us a great service.

5 star is not enough, I could give more if I could! Food portion servings were huge and affordable for an ambience like this! Great view of the river outside but I came when it was raining so I opted to sit at the building outside to have tea and sweets. Had dinner at the dining hall which was behind. The 149k VND tea set for 2 pax was the best experience ever! Peaceful surroundings with plants and background music, great deco and lighting, good tea and snacks!
Recommended when you’re in Hue!

The taste, the flavour, the balance, all just below par. They look amazing but just can't save the quality. reviews.text: We ate brunch at Nina’s cafe and loved it so much we just had to come back the next day again! The smoothie bowls and fresh juices were so refreshing, we couldn’t believe this amazing spot was just tucked away in a little alley very close to our hotel. Our waitresses, Nhi and Moon, were amazing: they made us feel very welcome and spoke great english as well. We couldn’t recommend this place more for a quick brunch!

If you are looking for the absolute best food in Vietnam, look no further than Nina’s Cafe. We came in for a late brunch that effortlessly turned into a long, delicious lunch—and honestly, we didn’t want to leave. After three weeks of traveling through the country, this was hands-down the best food and selection we’ve encountered.
​The atmosphere is incredibly relaxing and cozy, providing the perfect escape from the bustle of the city. However, what truly elevates this experience from a great meal to an unforgettable one is the hospitality. Our host, Ms. Lotus, was perfection. Her English is impeccable, and she is so much more than just a host; she is a cultural ambassador. She took the time to sit with us and educate us on the traditional way to prepare and eat each dish, adding a layer of depth to the meal that you just don't find elsewhere.
​We will be back again for sure. If you’re in Hue, do yourself a favor and find this hidden gem!

Finding Nina’s Cafe at the end of a long, quiet alleyway is half the fun—the other half is the incredible food and hospitality. This small, cozy spot is a peaceful escape from the main streets.

​The Service:
Huge shoutout to Lotus, who was a total powerhouse. She was the only server managing the entire restaurant single-handedly, yet she stayed welcoming, spoke excellent English, and took a genuine interest in our trip. Her recommendations were spot-on.

​The Standout Dishes:
​The BBQ Pork Noodles (Bun Thit Nuong): The pork had a fantastic flavor that reminded me of Filipino tocino, and the peanut sauce was the perfect finishing touch.

​Set 1: An absolute steal for the price. The Banh Beo was incredibly fresh, and the Banh Nam was a delicious highlight I’m glad we tried.

​Fried Fish: Light, crispy, and perfectly battered. It let the quality of the fish shine through instead of overpowering it.
​Grilled Lemon Chicken: This was "booming" with flavor—a massive hit with my son.

​If you want an authentic, quiet meal with top-tier service, make sure you find your way down the alley to this gem.

Nina’s café is a true gem, tucked away in a narrow street in central Hué. Do not hesitate to visit. The place feels fresh and welcoming, creating a lovely atmosphere from the moment you arrive.

Moon and N were extremely friendly and helped us choose our dishes with great care. They also speak excellent English, which is not always the case in many restaurants and cafés in Hué.

The food itself was delicious, beautifully presented, and very reasonably priced. The drinks were equally impressive, with great attention to detail in their presentation.

Highly recommended ☺️

One of our favourite restaurants of our trip - we ate here twice during our 2 nights in Hue. The caramel chicken hot pot is a must have but everything we tried was delicious.

reviews.text: Absolutely fantastic experience! The food here is insanely delicious, full of authentic flavor, and prepared with super fresh ingredients. I loved that they have great options for different dietary needs, including a dedicated gluten free menu and plenty of thoughtful vegan choices. We ordered a spread of amazing dishes and were blown away. The crispy Thai fried chicken served on banana leaf with kaffir lime leaves was incredible, and the fried chicken over rice with fresh cucumber slices was equally delicious. We also loved the stir fried noodles, the savory seafood fried rice with fresh lime wedges, and the cashew stir fry. Everything was packed with flavor, beautifully cooked, and loaded with fresh ingredients. Highly recommend this spot to anyone looking for amazing Thai food!

Really tasty Thai street food with vegan and veggie options, close to my accommodation - I came here a lot over my 10 days or so in Hue. Could easily eat here every day as it is so good - nourishing, healthy, generous portions and great value. Very handy as it stays open until 11pm, so if you’re back late or it’s rainy season, it’s perfect to have so close by. The service is fantastic and the meals are made so quickly, you can be in and out in 20-30 minutes usually. Everything was fresh to order and so delicious and you can see the cooks doing their thing in the kitchen. The place was always packed with locals and tourists alike but they will always find space for you. A great atmosphere as always busy, and you sit around quite communal with small tables close together and small chairs. They have a vegan menu of their regular dishes that can be adapted - so I had a lot of stir fried cashew nuts, tofu and vegetables on rice in various seasoning and sauces. They always check no fish sauce and no egg, and also ask your spice preference. Every combination I tried was 10/10. Very consistently good. They also sell bottled water and beers etc.

reviews.text: We stopped in for a late breakfast with the family and couldn’t have been happier with the choice. The food was delicious, hearty, and left us completely satisfied. Family Home Café & Restaurant was one of those happy discoveries in Hue that turned into a genuine favourite. We ended up eating here several times during our stay, which really says it all. When a place pulls you back that consistently, it's doing something right.

Rich, flavourful, and totally unexpected on a Vietnamese café menu — it works brilliantly and we'd order it every time. If you're spending time in Hue, put Family Home on your list early — that way you'll have plenty of chances to go back. Five stars without hesitation.

Mr. Pho was a great experience! It’s the perfect place to get a snack/breakfast before taking the train.
The food is fresh and delicious! I can really recommend the Banh Mi with Omelette. The coffee is delicious as well!

The owner is very welcoming and friendly. It’s a pleasure to chat with him.
I can highly recommend this place.

If you arrive in Huế by train, you might easily walk past this small and very unassuming place, but that would be a mistake. Mr Pho’s Pho and Cafe looks simple at first glance: plastic chairs, plastic tables, exactly what you would expect from a typical local Vietnamese spot. But behind that simplicity is truly great food.

The fried rice and fried noodles are excellent, fresh, flavorful, and perfect after a long journey. The prices are also very fair.

What really makes this place special, though, is Mr Pho himself. He takes great care of his guests, helps with train connections, gives travel tips, and if he has a moment, he even shares a few stories. You don’t feel like a customer there, you feel like a welcome guest.

It’s also very convenient for travelers: he offers to prepare food for your train journey and can store your luggage if you need to kill some time before your next train.

A genuine and authentic spot right next to the train station in Huế. Anyone passing through should definitely stop by.
★★★★★

Mr. Pho’s Café is a wonderful little spot located right across from the Hue railway station. The place is run by a very friendly and genuinely helpful owner, who makes the whole experience even better. The food is tasty, fresh, and prepared with great care.

One of the things I appreciated most is how thoughtful the owner is. Before taking your order, he asks which train you’re waiting for to make sure the meal is ready in time. You can also order your food packed for the journey, which is perfect if you’re about to catch a train.

Overall, it’s a warm, reliable, and delicious stop in Hue—highly recommended, especially for travelers passing through the station.
Delicious food, quick service, very reasonable prices, good vegetarian options. If you arrive by train, it's right in front of the station. And they provide welcome drinks too! Highly recommended.

The guy who runs this establishment (maybe Mr Pho himself?) couldn't be any nicer. Located right by the train station, he looked after our bags for a very reasonable fee while we spent a day in Hue. He checked when our train was leaving, and told us which platform / waiting room we needed to be in. He was so nice and trusting, he voluntarily lent us cash because we'd run out, and said we could pay him back when we returned at the end of the day.

Because of his generosity, we stayed for a drink and some food, before heading towards the Imperial City. The banh mi were tasty and very reasonably priced.

Thank you for helping to make our visit to Vietnam an even better experience!
Mr Pho is one of the kindest person I've ever met, very helpful and nice. 100% recommended for storing luggage, eating or just traveling information.

I had stored my luggage with his family for a super reasonable fee, he takes his job seriously and I was so thankful to have met them.

reviews.text:
We visited Hue Imperial City and were looking for a halal-friendly restaurant nearby for lunch. We were very pleased to find An Nhien Garden Vegetarian.

The restaurant has a beautiful and peaceful ambience, with very friendly and helpful staff. The food was tasty and enjoyable.

A special thanks to Assistant Manager Hien Phu, who was very kind and helpful in arranging an alternative prayer area for us when the permanent prayer area was under maintenance. We truly appreciated the thoughtful hospitality and understanding.

Highly recommended for anyone visiting Hue, especially Muslim travellers looking for a welcoming and comfortable dining experience. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

What an absolutely beautiful and delicious restaurant. Don’t hesitate and book a table or make your way there now. The food was incredibly fresh and tasty but everything there has a wonderful back story to it. From the impetus for establishing the restaurant to the 400+ years of family legacy, there is so much to this place that you will not regret your decision to dine here.

The velvet apple or Hong Nhung was incredible if it’s in season when you’re there it’s a must. One of the best fruits I’ve ever tasted.

A truly hidden (!) gem. This is one of the must surprising, yet magical locations we‘ve seen in Vietnam. It‘s a backyard garden of a victorian style villa. My wife and my two kids loved it. Food was fantastic and not expensive. Perfect for everyone who‘s staying at the Kobi Onsen Resort.

I wish I had found this place on my last trip, but was super stoked to have found it on this trip to Hue.

The restaurant is set up in a garden with tables set up around it as well.

We started off sitting in the garden but there were some mosquitos so we moved away from the lush garden setting. Probably something that's hard to get away from as the weather warms up.

We ordered several platters with many things to try. One of my favorites was from "Hue on a Tray" where three different "banh" were offered. The black sesame item was exceptional both in taste and texture.

We also ordered the "Traditional Hue Meal" which included rice, veggies, tofu, soup, and a very unique pickled eggplant dish.

The Pomelo Salad was also very tasty.

I suggest making a reservation as the restaurant, though not full, was rather busy on a weeknight.

This is an incredible vegeterain place to eat. Caters for vegans and halal. Its the venue that makes the amazing food taste even better. The service is top notch. The meals in the pictures look smaller than they are, you might over-order.

Incredibly peaceful vegetarian/vegan garden refuge in the middle of Hue. The moment u walk in, you are greeted by hanging orchids, beautiful paintings, statue-adorned zen garden pathways, accompanied by the relaxing sound of water, leaves rustling, and birds singing along with cicadas. It's literally another world.

The staff was honest, polite & knowledgeable, so much that my aunt wanted to adopt one of them.

Although they are mostly vegan, some dishes may have milk, so make sure you ask the staff first. We were told everything on the menu can be made vegan. If you let them know first, they will not add dairy.

The food was amazing, well-presented & full of flavor even tho they emphasize the health aspect of food. Everything was freshly prepared with minimal processing.

If u happen to stop by Hue, pls visit An Nhien Garden to rest and enjoy incredible food.

The atmosphere is so refreshing — surrounded by trees, plants, and a lovely garden that makes you feel completely connected to nature. It’s the kind of place where you can relax, take a deep breath, and just enjoy the moment.

The menu offers a wonderful selection, especially for those who enjoy vegetarian and healthy options. There’s something for everyone, and it’s clear that the ingredients are fresh and thoughtfully prepared. Our food was served quickly, beautifully decorated, and most importantly — absolutely delicious!

The garden area is definitely the highlight, creating such a calm and natural vibe that perfectly complements the meal. Whether you’re dining solo, with friends, or as a couple, it’s an ideal place to unwind and enjoy good food in a lovely setting.
